description: Explorers from another planet seeking creativity in the galaxy
summary:
Project statement:

Ever wondered how an astronaut survives on a subsurface ocean world and repairs their ship to make it home? Say less we, Team Tridiods, created Europa Abyss Protocol for the NASA Space Apps Challenge to bridge the gap between realistic space engineering and engaging gameplay.

Our solution:

Traditional sci-fi games often ignore real space physics, leaving students with an abstract view of engineering trade-offs. Our interactive simulation puts players directly into an astronaut’s boots on Europa. Players must manage limited resources, navigate low-gravity Extravehicular Activity (EVA) physics, and balance suit thermal limits against hostile extremophiles. Instead of simple button-presses, players perform realistic diagnostics to repair Environmental Control and Life Support System (ECLSS) hardware like Sabatier reactors and CO₂ scrubbers.To ensure scientific accuracy, we built our game using NASA Europa Clipper datasets for the icy ocean environment, NASA ECLSS documentation for life-support mechanics, and NASA Astrobiology research to model realistic bioluminescent creatures and hydrothermal vents.

Our impact:

Ultimately, this simulation transforms complex aerospace engineering into a fun, hands-on learning tool—inspiring the next generation to understand real space physics and what it truly takes to survive off-world.
details:
Europa Abyss Protocol is an interactive space-survival simulation set beneath the icy crust of Jupiter’s moon, Europa. Players step into an astronaut’s boots to repair damaged Environmental Control and Life Support System (ECLSS) hardware—including Sabatier reactors, CO₂ scrubbers, and hull breaches—using realistic diagnostics while navigating low-gravity Extravehicular Activity (EVA) physics, rationing monopropellant fuel, and surviving hostile extremophiles to transmit a final signal back to Earth.

By turning real aerospace engineering trade-offs into high-stakes action, the project bridges the gap between overly abstract educational simulations and unrealistic sci-fi games. Our intended impact is to transform complex spaceflight mechanics and astrobiology into an intuitive, hands-on learning experience that inspires the next generation of space explorers and engineers.

We built the prototype using Makeplay AI and official NASA datasets from Europa Clipper, ECLSS engineering manuals, and astrobiology extremophile research. Also, we turned vacuum thermodynamics where thrusters, tools, and weapons accumulate dangerous suit heat into fight and combat mechanics, paired with bioluminescent creatures grounded in real chemosynthetic vent data. Finally, our team carefully balanced scientific accuracy, resource limits, accessible pacing, and modular architecture to support future two-player cooperative gameplay.
